local.b: A $28 billion hemp THC market faces elimination after Congress voted to close the loophole that let it grow.

local.h: All six lost in Nantucket air ambulance named
local.b: Officials identified the six people aboard the air ambulance that crashed off Nantucket on a flight from Bermuda to Boston.
more: Passengers were Marilyn Lavonne Bean, 66, and her son Sergio Wayne Lottimore, 41, of Bermuda; the four crew were Canadian.
The Coast Guard suspended its search Sunday after 66 hours.

local.h: Jury selection begins in Birchmore murder trial
local.b: Jury selection starts in the trial of former Stoughton detective Matthew Farwell, accused of killing Sandra Birchmore in 2021.
more: Prosecutors say he abused her from age 15 in a police youth program, then killed her to keep her from reporting it.
Farwell has pleaded not guilty and maintains she took her own life.

local.h: Healey declares a home 'energy emergency'
local.b: Gov. Healey raised heating aid and ordered cuts to some electric bill charges as heating oil prices rose 73% in a year.
more: She said one in five Massachusetts households heat with oil.

local.h: Clergy abuse report puts focus on Beacon Hill
local.b: Attorney General Andrea Campbell urged lawmakers to end the statute of limitations on civil child sex abuse claims.

local.b: The Aurora native rose to House speaker before a 2016 conviction revealed he had sexually abused teenage boys as a wrestling coach.

local.h: Bob Odenkirk heads back to the stage
local.b: The Naperville native is turning to theater, with plans for a production in Champaign.

local.h: Runner set for his 48th Chicago Marathon
local.b: A retired systems analyst, one of two people to finish every Chicago Marathon since 1977, will run again in his high school gym shorts.

goodnews.b: Community leaders raised $75 million to develop nine Bronzeville sites, including a theater and a food hub.

goodnews.h: White Sox go from worst to the playoffs
goodnews.b: Two years after being baseball's worst team, the White Sox are in the playoffs and won their division series opener.

local.h: Hiking Whittier's history with the 'Lumpers'
local.b: A retired women's hiking group toured Whittier's parks named for Black historical figures like Madam C.J. Walker.

local.h: Denver weighs what to do with empty offices
local.b: Downtown Denver's office vacancy is 38%, and old buildings are costly to convert or tear down.

local.h: Hilton makes GOP pitch at LA Times-LAist forum
local.b: Republican governor candidate Steve Hilton takes questions from LA journalists Tuesday at a forum co-hosted by the LA Times and LAist.
more: It streams at 4 p.m. and re-airs on LAist 89.3 FM at 7 p.m.
Moderators plan to ask about housing, homelessness, climate change and ties with the federal government.

local.h: FBI arrests Irvine woman in China spying case
local.b: The FBI arrested real estate agent Wanying Zhang at LAX, accusing her of spying on Taiwan's president's son for China.

local.h: New rules for buying a car in California
local.b: Since October 1, California requires clearer upfront pricing when you buy a car, KQED reports.

local.h: Newport Beach voters may get two ballots
local.b: Newport Beach is scrambling to hold its own court-ordered election alongside November's general election.

local.h: Newsom vetoes towed-car money bill
local.b: Newsom vetoed a bill that would have made the DMV hand over leftover proceeds from sales of towed cars to their owners.

local.h: Fact check: Newsom's CARE Court numbers
local.b: Newsom said CARE Court helped 10,000+ Californians, but state data shows 1,470 with treatment agreements or plans as of June.

local.h: South LA hears District 9 council candidates
local.b: Candidates Jose Ugarte and Estuardo Mazariegos laid out plans on housing, transit and safety at a forum held in extreme heat.

local.h: Hochul declares measles 'disaster emergency'
local.b: Gov. Hochul declared a disaster emergency as measles spreads across rural upstate New York.

local.h: Relief for NYC tenants losing rent vouchers
local.b: Nearly 6,300 NYC households losing federal rental aid may get to replace their vouchers and stay in their apartments.
more: HUD issued new guidance after letting the earlier aid expire caused fear among tenants and landlords.

local.h: Blind man cut from grand jury can sue NY
local.b: A judge ruled a blind man dismissed from a Brooklyn grand jury can sue New York for discrimination.
more: Albert Elia, 52, says the judge barred him from voting on cases with visual evidence and denied accommodations.

local.h: Gatorade recall reaches New York and New Jersey
local.b: More than 122,000 cases of Gatorade in 37 states are recalled because some bottles may contain unlisted food dyes.

local.h: NYPD detective forced out over false statements
local.b: A Brooklyn detective who admitted giving false information in an investigation was forced to retire after 18 years.

local.h: Pressure on Mamdani to fix Hunts Point market
local.b: Advocates want the mayor to revive a $650 million plan to cut diesel pollution at the South Bronx produce market.
more: The market supplies up to 60% of the city's fruits and vegetables.

local.h: Cyclist dies after hitting off-leash dog in Central Park
local.b: A 71-year-old cyclist died after colliding with an unleashed dog on East Drive near 84th Street Monday morning, police said.

local.h: Two Legionnaires' cases at Queens housing complex
local.b: Two North Shore Towers residents were diagnosed with Legionnaires' disease, and the Health Department is investigating.

local.h: Man who shot border officer gets 15 years
local.b: A man who shot an off-duty Customs and Border Protection officer in a botched robbery in Fort Washington Park was sentenced to 15 years.

goodnews.h: American chestnut returns to the Bronx Zoo
goodnews.b: The Bronx Zoo is getting 25 blight-resistant chestnut saplings to help restore a tree nearly wiped out for over a century.

goodnews.h: Late-night soccer returns to five NYC parks
goodnews.b: One soccer field in each borough will stay lit until 2 a.m. this fall and next spring, after a summer pilot drew 4,500 players.

local.h: Students march across Paris in school protests
local.b: High school students march in Paris Tuesday from Place de la Republique to Place de la Nation in a third national day of protests.
more: Students protest teacher shortages, scarce resources and crumbling school buildings.
Roads and some Metro stations along Boulevard Voltaire are closed.

local.h: French unions call nationwide strike Nov. 5
local.b: French unions called a day of cross-sector strikes and protests on Thursday, November 5th.
more: The CFDT, CGT, FO, Unsa and FSU unions back the call 'for wages, public services, employment and industry.'
The government faces growing opposition to its draft 2027 budget.

local.h: Teen protester loses hand to police grenade
local.b: A 15-year-old in Lens lost his hand Monday when a police sting-ball grenade exploded during a school protest.

local.h: France to suspend licences for phone use at wheel
local.b: Drivers caught using a handheld phone will face licence suspensions nationwide after local pilot schemes.

local.h: Single train-and-plane ticket extends to Ouigo
local.b: Air France and SNCF's combined Train + Air ticket now covers some low-cost Ouigo trains to Paris-Charles de Gaulle.

local.h: Poll: WA trans sports ban measure could pass
local.b: Polling shows a Washington ballot measure banning trans girls from girls' school sports could pass in November.
more: Voters decide the measure in the November election.

local.h: Supreme Court orders new look at WA political maps
local.b: The court sent a challenge to Washington's legislative maps back to a lower court; it won't affect next month's election.

local.h: Snohomish firefighters lose vaccine mandate case
local.b: The Supreme Court declined to hear eight Snohomish County firefighters who refused the COVID vaccine on religious grounds.

local.h: DelBene predicts Democrats will win the House
local.b: Rep. Suzan DelBene, who leads House Democrats' campaign arm, predicted her party will win a House majority in November.
